correspondence.finding: The western approach follows the broadly eastward North Fork corridor toward Hunt. TPWD Figure 12 and the GBRA poster distinguish this route from the South Fork arriving from the southwest and Johnson Creek arriving from the north. The short headmost feeder is not individually named, and the modeled start is not asserted to be a named spring or surveyed source.

Beyond Hunt, the line continues east through the Ingram and Kerrville corridor, bends southeast toward Center Point and continues east through Kendall County. The Kerr County map resolves the upper sequence, while the statewide map and basin poster carry the same channel onward. The separate Johnson Creek and South Fork labels are not transferred downstream as aliases.

The winding eastward Hill Country reach passes through the Canyon Reservoir setting and turns south toward New Braunfels before bending east again toward Seguin. The poster and TPWD river map reproduce this distinctive turn. TPWD's waterways account independently separates the reservoir, downstream Guadalupe and Comal tributary; an impoundment passage is not treated as a river-name synonym.

The eastward continuation past Seguin reaches Gonzales, turns predominantly south toward Cuero and then southeast through the Victoria corridor. These successive bends match the labeled Guadalupe on both regional maps. San Marcos, Coleto Creek and the San Antonio River remain separately mapped contributing waterways, rather than alternative names for the selected trunk.

The last southeastward continuation and short second fragment occupy the Guadalupe coastal approach at the head of the San Antonio Bay system. The GBRA poster depicts the lower river, its separate San Antonio tributary and estuarine continuation; TWDB independently states the receiving bay. Map scale does not resolve every terminal distributary or establish the modeled endpoint as a precise contemporary river mouth.

The headward eastward extension occupies the Little Mulberry feeder setting. The county original depicts Little Mulberry River separately from the Apalachee drainage, including its eastward passage toward Barrow County. This supports upper contributing-stream context, not an Altamaha name for the headwater endpoint or an exact mapped name-transition vertex.

The path then turns south through the upper Oconee corridor and reservoir chain. EPA text explicitly distinguishes Oconee River below the North and Middle Oconee confluence from the reach continuing to Lake Oconee; NOAA places Sinclair on this eastern trunk. Upper feeders and Lake Oconee/Sinclair remain separate features.

Below the reservoir corridor, the selected mainstem follows the south-southeast Oconee side to the two-river junction. The two western contributing pieces match the separately mapped Ocmulgee corridor and its broad lower eastward bend. NOAA text identifies their confluence as the start of Altamaha River.

From that junction the lower selected piece proceeds east and then southeast. The DNR original river guide follows the same trunk past the Ohoopee junction and the Jesup/Jaycee Landing setting toward Fort Barrington. Ohoopee and the surrounding creeks are separate tributaries, not aliases of this group.

The final approach enters the branching tidal setting near Darien. The DNR guide separates Darien and Champney landing/channel context; the EPD description places the terminal waters in Altamaha Sound. The simplified model endpoint is not assigned an exact distributary, estuarine boundary or surveyed ocean-mouth vertex.

The modeled southern start lies in the lake country southwest of Winisk Lake. Its northward approach, westward bend and subsequent northeast continuation reach the Winisk lake corridor shown on the original map. The map labels Fishbasket and Mameigwess in this upper setting, but its scale does not resolve the initial small feeder or authorize assigning one river name or exact lake entry/exit points to the entire modeled piece.

The long western contribution corresponds to the eastward Wunnummin lake-chain approach and the adjoining complex of channels and lakes toward Winisk. The original separately depicts Wunnummin, Chipai, Wapikopa, Kanuchuan and Winisk lakes; their mapped spatial arrangement and connecting channels distinguish this contribution from the more northerly Asheweig drainage. Lake names are preserved as waterbody context, not treated as aliases for all selected connecting lines.

The selected junction near the northern Winisk Lake corridor continues north along the map’s directly labeled Winisk River. The subsequent eastern bulge and return north agree with the mapped trunk. The separately drawn and labeled Winiskisti Channel east of the upper trunk is not adopted as the name of the whole selection; model-fragment boundaries are not name boundaries.

The short western contribution follows the lower north-turning tributary corridor below the mapped Asheweig/Frog junction and into Winisk. The map’s connected Asheweig course and the intervening Muzhikoba Creek confluence distinguish it from the Winisk trunk. Asheweig is retained as contributing-river context, without extending that name to the full group or forcing names onto every small incoming stream.

The named Winisk trunk continues north, makes the pronounced eastward turn, and then bends northeast into a widened estuarine channel at Hudson Bay. The original shows the same lower-river bend sequence, the separate Mishamattawa approach, and the coastal setting between Wabuk Point and Flagstaff Point. The modeled final point is within this estuarine mouth area; the regional sheet does not fix the exact contemporary shoreline, tidal limit or terminal channel vertex.

correspondence: The complete single selected fragment was inspected from its southern interior endpoint through the long nearly straight northern leg, the short northwestward upper-margin sequence and final northern extension. No additional tributary fragment is present.

The long southern and middle route lies on mapped Inland Ice. Its northern approach reaches the ice-margin and Victoria Fjord setting. The original map graticule and ice/land/fjord arrangement, supported by the accompanying map-label register, distinguish this from neighboring fjords; proximity to the label is not treated as river-name evidence.

The original does not establish the entire path as a named surface river, subglacial river or glacier. A line continuing into a fjord cannot inherit the fjord name as a river identity, and the exact terminal natural-feature boundary remains unassigned.

Surface, ice-thickness and sub-ice bedrock contours describe the ice and terrain, not named river channels. Historical mapping supplies regional context without proving present flow, connectivity or current ice-front position.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
